stimulus.source_note: Description of a 1950s Ford automobile advertisement, rebuilt from the staged survivor 5s24-exam1-mcq-27; the advertisement image is not reproduced.
stimulus.text: A 1950s Ford automobile advertisement shows a smiling suburban family loading luggage into a gleaming new car parked before their ranch house. The copy celebrates the car's new fins and glittering chrome, the yearly model change, and easy credit terms for buyers.

stem: The advertisement's emphasis on yearly model changes and easy credit best shows which change in the postwar economy?

options.text: Car makers turned the car into a mass good bought on credit
Automobile makers stopped advertising and sold cars only by word of mouth
options.misconception: Background from the books: the 1950s advertising industry boomed and stoked demand for new cars.

options.text: Most families paid cash for cars and refused to borrow
options.misconception: Background from the books: credit cards and easy credit terms spread in the postwar years so families could buy now and pay later.

options.text: The government banned yearly model changes to save steel
options.misconception: Background from the books: makers celebrated yearly model changes with fins and chrome; no ban stopped them.

rationales.A: New fins every year plus easy credit terms mean cars were sold as fashion bought on borrowed money, not as rare luxuries.
rationales.B: Background from the books: advertising in the 1950s reached levels last seen in the 1920s and stoked demand for new cars.
rationales.C: Background from the books: credit spread after the war, and the ad itself boasts of easy credit terms for buyers.
rationales.D: Background from the books: makers celebrated yearly model changes with fins and chrome; no ban on model changes existed.
rationales.general:
1. Read the ad as a sales pitch: what is it selling besides a car? Newness every year, and borrowing to pay for it.
2. Background from the books: a rejuvenated advertising industry helped stoke demand, and credit cards became a popular way to buy.
3. Together, yearly newness and easy credit turn a car from a rare purchase into a mass good bought on credit.
Remember: When an ad sells the payment plan, credit is part of the product.
